text:
lina_support: heads-up — ACME (acct: acme-inc) flagged invoice INV-2026-09-183. Invoice shows 3,184,512 tokens for Aug 24-25 but their dashboard totals ~1,078,302. customer asked for explanation + refund. sample request ids they pasted: req_8a1, req_8a2, req_8b7. can eng/billing triage?

sam_ing: on it. which model & exact time window? any evidence of client retries? please paste raw request logs or sample timestamps.

lina_support: model: redwood/gtl-13b (hosted). window: 2026-08-24T22:45 -> 2026-08-25T03:00 UTC. pasted two raw lines from their logs (redacted):

```
2026-08-25T00:12:03Z req=req_8a1 status=200 tokens_in=512 tokens_out=128 client_retries=0
2026-08-25T00:12:04Z req=req_8a1 status=200 tokens_in=512 tokens_out=128 client_retries=1
```

They say their app retried once on timeout but kept the same X-Request-Id. I also grabbed our ingress logs where I see duplicate meter entries for the same user/time.

sam_ing: thanks. uploading quick query results from metering DB (note: returning counts per request-id):

```
SELECT request_id, count(*) FROM metering.events WHERE account_id='acme-inc' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-08-24' AND '2026-08-25' GROUP BY request_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 5;
# result: req_8a1 -> 2, req_8a2 -> 2, req_8b7 -> 1
```

sam_ing: initial hypothesis — our aggregator v1.2.3 dedupes on trace_id but not X-Request-Id; when client retries with NEW trace_id but reuses the same X-Request-Id, we sometimes count both. triggering path seems to be timeouts + client retry pattern.

billing-bot: automated-meter-audit: found high correlation between client retry spikes and duplicated meter entries for acct acme-inc. flagged 2,106,210 tokens suspected double-counted (approx). Suggested action: manual audit + provisional credit.

maria_finance: thanks. rough numbers please — what's the $ impact? need a finance-approved refund amount and revrec note. also need GL account to post adjustment.

sam_ing: calculation: suspected double-counted tokens = 2,106,210. hosted rate for gtl-13b during period = $0.0004/token -> gross = $842.484. propose rounding to $842.48 credit. Patch PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/3214 (dedupe on X-Request-Id for 72h, backfill protection). patch passed CI, queued for hotfix deploy.

maria_finance: ok — approve provisional credit of $842.48. finance ticket FIN-19874 created for audit & revrec. RevRec note draft: "Metering duplicate counting due to retry dedupe bug in metering aggregator v1.2.3; credit issued to customer INV-2026-09-183. GL: 410-REFUND-XX." Please attach the metering query & billing-bot audit.

lina_support: I messaged the customer with the explanation + proposed $842.48 credit; they accepted. I initiated refund via Stripe and created invoice adjustment. Stripe refund ID: r_5KxZ. finance posted adjustment to account and updated invoice notes.

raj_pm: good catch — need follow-ups: 1) add alert for invoice vs dashboard variance >20% (account-level), 2) add doc guidance for clients to set Idempotency-Key or stable X-Request-Id, 3) run backfill audit for last 30 days and flag other potential impacted accounts. pls coordinate.

sam_ing: follow-ups: hotfix deployed to metering aggregator (v1.2.4) with dedupe window 72h, soft rollout to region-us-west2 first. added unit tests + end-to-end for retry patterns. I kicked off a backfill job to re-evaluate past 30 days — initial scan queued (job id backfill-20260825-01).

billing-bot: audit & adjustment posted: -$842.48 applied to INV-2026-09-183. revrec note: "Metering double-count due to retry dedupe bug; refund issued." Finance ticket FIN-19874 linked.

lina_support: customer confirmed credit applied and replied \"thanks, that fixes it\" :white_check_mark:. closing from support side; tagging engineering & finance to follow through on alerts + backfill.

sam_ing: I'll follow up in eng-runtime with rollout schedule and backfill results.

maria_finance: closing FIN ticket once backfill audit confirms no further adjustments needed.

lina_support: closing thread — final status: refund issued $842.48, FIN-19874, hotfix deployed, backfill running.
